chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! Begin your meal with salt and end with salt, for whoever begins his meal with salt and ends with it, Allah will repel from him seventy types of afflictions, the easiest of which is leprosy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical benefit of starting and ending a meal with salt according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Prophetic tradition of using salt as a spiritual and physical safeguard, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between bodily health and divine protection. The promise of deliverance from seventy afflictions, with leprosy as the least severe, underscores the comprehensive nature of this simple act of worship. This practice is often viewed by scholars as both a means of preserving health and a reminder of God's mercy in daily sustenance.
